answer: Use sequential-compute identity proofs. At registration, each key must compute a slow memory-hard hash chain seeded by its public key and the latest block, taking about six hours on one core and not parallelizable. Every day it must publish a short pulse, the next chain checkpoint, which verifiers spot-check cheaply. A hollow key that skips work misses checkpoints and loses its seat. A lotus of one thousand fakes needs one dedicated core each, costing roughly two dollars daily per identity.
